cases.name: router-prd-first
cases.promptMarkdown: /ask-codingforux My product manager just sent me a PRD for a new team invites feature. I haven't done anything with it yet. Which skill do I run first?

graders.name: first-step-is-grill-prd
graders.graderMarkdown:
PASS if the reply tells the user that the first skill to run on the PRD is grill-prd (written as `grill-prd` or `/grill-prd`).
FAIL if it names a different skill as the first step, lists several skills without saying which comes first, or never names grill-prd.

graders.name: first-step-is-grill-prd
graders.evidence:
Run **`/grill-prd`** first.

Paste the PRD into it, or pass a file, doc link, or tracker issue. It will:

- Interview you to sharpen your understanding of the team invites PRD.
- Read only the personas the PRD affects.
- Mark each PRD item **yours**, **not yours**, or **needs alignment**.
- Park any question only your team can answer as a `needs-alignment` sub-issue.

**What comes next**
- **Anything parked?** Run `/to-ux-questionnaire`. It gathers the open questions into one message. You send it to your PM, since the agent never messages anyone. If the PM replies with a new PRD draft instead of answers, re-run `/grill-prd`.
- **Nothing parked?** Go straight to `/to-ux-brief`.

If this is your first flow on this product, run `/setup-codingforux-skills` once beforehand. It checks that the Figma MCP can write and sets up the folders, tracker, labels, standards, and personas the other skills assume.

Try to keep `/grill-prd`, the questionnaire, `/to-ux-brief`, and `/to-ux-tickets` in one unbroken context window, so each step builds on the same thinking.
